title: Compass, Straightedge & Vesica — Dual-Axis Geometry Atlas
purpose: Extract exact compass-and-straightedge consequences from the project's vesica/mandorla geometry and correct an orientation ambiguity in the existing canonical coordinate model.
epistemic_rule: All geometric identities below follow from ordinary Euclidean geometry. Symbolic assignments such as Father, Son, Door, Plane or Axis are project overlays; no angle or ratio proves a theological identity or ancient hidden code.
vesica_definition: Two equal circles of radius r whose centers are separated by exactly r form the standard vesica piscis. Each circle center lies on the circumference of the other.

stacked_center_model.correction: This coordinate arrangement is a valid vesica with vertically stacked Father/Son centers, but the lens itself is horizontally elongated. It should be named a stacked-center Father/Son overlap rather than a vertically elongated mandorla.
stacked_center_model.endpoint_note: C_F and C_S are top/bottom extrema of the overlap because each is on the other circle, but the actual circle-circle intersection points are P_L and P_R. The latter are where the two boundary arcs meet.

vertical_mandorla_model.project_use: If the visual requirement is a tall/vertical almond-shaped Door or mandorla, this is the orientation to use. The two source-circle centers sit left/right while the Door's long axis rises vertically between them.

dual_axis_principle.center_axis: the straight line joining the two circle centers
dual_axis_principle.door_axis: the common chord through the two circle-intersection points
dual_axis_principle.theorem: For equal intersecting circles, the center line and common chord are perpendicular and share the same midpoint O.
dual_axis_principle.project_epiphany: The geometry naturally supplies two orthogonal axes: one relates the two generating centers; the other runs through the shared overlap/threshold. The project should therefore distinguish generator/source relation from passage/Door direction instead of forcing one line to perform both jobs.
dual_axis_principle.warning: Geometry does not decide which project roles belong on which axis; that assignment must come from the chronology/canon.

equilateral_triangle_structure.construction: Take either intersection point P together with the two circle centers. Since both radii and the center separation equal r, the triangle has sides r,r,r.
equilateral_triangle_structure.angles: All three interior angles are exactly 60 degrees.
consequences: the vesica contains exact equilateral-triangle structure
the sqrt(3) lens dimension follows from the altitude of an equilateral triangle

intersection_angles.radii: At either circle intersection, the two radii to the centers meet at 60 degrees.
intersection_angles.tangents: Each tangent is perpendicular to its corresponding radius, so the two tangent lines also meet with acute angle 60 degrees; the supplementary angle is 120 degrees.
intersection_angles.project_use: 60/120 is an exact local boundary-angle property of this construction. It can be indexed as geometry, but should not be retrofitted into scripture, Masonry, 666, or other traditions without historical evidence.

lens_area.invariance: Rotating the entire vesica changes orientation but not area, angle structure or intrinsic ratios.

steps: Choose two points A and B separated by the chosen radius r.
Draw a circle centered at A through B.
Without changing compass radius, draw a circle centered at B through A.
Mark the two circle intersections P and Q.
Draw PQ; it is the common chord and perpendicular bisector of AB.
Draw AB; its intersection with PQ is midpoint O.
ruler_compass_construction.epiphany: A pair of equal-status points plus one conserved length is enough to generate midpoint, perpendicularity, a second axis, 60-degree structure, sqrt(3), and the lens/threshold. No protractor or arbitrary angle choice is needed.

golden_spiral_cross_overlay.quirky_insight: The compass vesica naturally produces 60-degree angular increments, while the project spiral is calibrated to 90-degree golden-ratio scaling. Overlaying them creates a 30-degree common angular subdivision. After twelve 30-degree steps the direction returns to its start while radius has grown by phi^4.
golden_spiral_cross_overlay.stronger_insight: The spiral therefore demonstrates exact angular return without spatial return: after 360 degrees the direction is the same but the scale is different. This is a rigorous mathematical instance of 'return at another level' inside the project's own recovered equation.
golden_spiral_cross_overlay.boundary: The 60-degree/90-degree overlay is a new mathematical analysis. It is not evidence that the original spiral was designed from the vesica, that phi is encoded in Jachin/Boaz, or that an ancient tradition contained this combined construction.

derived_objects: mirror/reflection symmetry exchanging A and B
paired_point_generalization.threshold_interpretation: Two flankers can define a center and an approach/passage axis even when neither flanker is the center or Door.
paired_point_generalization.warning: Similarity of a two-sided diagram is not evidence that all paired symbols historically derive from one another.

implementation_correction.recommendation: Preserve its existing stacked Father/Son coordinates as a valid project geometry, but explicitly label it 'stacked-center orientation'. Add a separate rotated 'vertical-mandorla orientation' for artwork/UI requiring a tall Door.
implementation_correction.visual_rule: Always specify whether 'vertical' refers to the line of circle centers or the long axis of the lens. They are perpendicular in a standard vesica and cannot both be vertical simultaneously.

sources.topic: vesica exact dimensions, equilateral triangles and area
